events.fact: Xero provides five pricing tiers for developers based on connection count and monthly data egress: Starter (5 connections, free, no security assessment required initially, 1,000 calls/day/org limit), Core (50 connections, $35 AUD/mo, 10 GB egress), Plus (1,000 connections, $245 AUD/mo, 50 GB egress), Advanced (10,000 connections, $1,445 AUD/mo, 250 GB egress, unlocks journals/XPM/bulk connections), and Enterprise (Unlimited connections, pricing on application). Overage egress is $2.40 AUD per GB.

Xero API rate limits per organization/tenant connection are: 5 concurrent calls, 60 calls per minute, and 5,000 calls per day (Starter plan has 1,000 calls per day). App-wide minute limit is 10,000 calls per minute across all tenants.
Xero updated its Developer Terms and Conditions (effective March 2, 2026 for existing developers) to explicitly prohibit using API data to train AI/ML models.

Xero introduced granular scopes starting March 2, 2026. Apps created on/after that date use granular scopes automatically, while existing apps have until September 2027 to migrate. Calling an endpoint without the required granular scope returns a 401 with WWW-Authenticate: insufficient_scope.
Xero requires absolute URIs for OAuth 2.0 redirect URIs (no wildcards) and allows registering up to 50 unique redirect URIs per app.
Xero app certification requires onboarding 10 beta customers actively using the integration (API calls in the last 30 days) and completing an initial security assessment.
The authorize endpoint is https://login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize and returns unauthorized_client when called with an unverified or fake client ID.

events.fact: Xero access tokens expire after 30 minutes, and refresh tokens expire after 60 days of non-use. Each refresh returns a new refresh token that must be stored.
Xero supports PKCE for applications that cannot securely store a client secret.
